title: Πίθηξ καὶ ἁλιεῖς
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 304. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Πίθηξ ἔν τινι ὑψηλῷ δένδρῳ καθήμενος, ὡς ἐθεάσατο ἁλιεῖς ἐπί τινος ποταμοῦ σαγήνην βάλλοντας, παρετήρει τὰ ὑπ’ αὐτῶν γινόμενα.
sentences.tr: Pithēx en tini hypsēlōi dendrōi kathēmenos, hōs etheasato halieis epi tinos potamou sagēnēn ballontas, paretērei ta hyp’ autōn ginomena.
sentences.l: A monkey, sitting in a high tree, when he saw fishermen casting a drag-net on a river, watched closely the things being done by them.
sentences.i: A monkey sitting high in a tree saw fishermen casting a drag-net on a river, and watched closely what they were doing.
sentences.n: A σαγήνη is the great drag-net hauled through the water between two parties of men, not a hand-net — which is why one monkey cannot manage it. θεάομαι takes the supplementary participle βάλλοντας: he saw them in the act of casting. παρατηρέω is to watch narrowly from beside.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ τούτων τὴν σαγήνην ἐασάντων, καὶ μικρὸν ὑποχωρησάντων τοῦ φαγεῖν, καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ δένδρου, ἐπειρᾶτο μιμεῖσθαι αὐτούς· φασὶ γὰρ μιμητικὸν εἶναι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο.
sentences.tr: Kai dē toutōn tēn sagēnēn easantōn, kai mikron hypochōrēsantōn tou phagein, katabas apo tou dendrou, epeirato mimeisthai autous· phasi gar mimētikon einai to zōion touto.
sentences.l: And indeed, when these had left the net and had withdrawn a little to eat, he, having come down from the tree, tried to imitate them; for they say that this animal is given to imitation.
sentences.i: And when they had left the net and gone off a little way to eat, he came down from the tree and set about imitating them — for this animal, they say, is a great mimic.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute again, and a double one. τοῦ φαγεῖν is an articular infinitive in the genitive doing the work of a purpose clause, 'for the eating'. The aside φασί, 'they say', is the teller stepping out of the story to vouch for a fact about monkeys — the collection does this rarely.

sentences.t: Ἐφαψάμενος δὲ τῶν δικτύων καὶ συλληφθεὶς ἐκινδύνευε πνιγῆναι.
sentences.tr: Ephapsamenos de tōn diktyōn kai syllēphtheis ekindyneue pnigēnai.
sentences.l: But having laid hold of the nets and having been taken in them, he was in danger of being choked.
sentences.i: But he laid hold of the nets, was caught fast in them, and was in danger of drowning.
sentences.n: ἐφάπτομαι takes the genitive of what it lays hold of. συλλαμβάνω, 'gather together', is the word for a net closing on its catch, and it is used of the monkey exactly as of a fish. κινδυνεύω with the infinitive is 'run the risk of', as at fable 297; πνίγω is to choke, and in water, to drown.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἔφη· « Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε δίκαια πέπονθα· τί γὰρ ἁλιεύειν μὴ μαθὼν τούτῳ ἐπεχείρουν ; »
sentences.tr: Ho de pros heauton ephē· « All’ egōge dikaia pepontha· ti gar halieuein mē mathōn toutōi epecheiroun ; »
sentences.l: But he said to himself: « Well, I for my part have suffered just things; for why, not having learned to fish, was I setting my hand to this? »
sentences.i: But he said to himself: « Well, it serves me right; why was I taking up a trade I had never learned? »
sentences.n: δίκαια πέπονθα, 'I have suffered what is just', is the collection's set phrase of self-reproach, spoken word for word by the shepherd at fable 229. ἐπεχείρουν is imperfect, of the attempt still in progress when it went wrong, and ἐπιχειρέω takes the dative τούτῳ.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι ἡ τῶν μηδὲν προσηκόντων ἐπιχείρησις οὐ μόνον ἀσύμφορος, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐπιβλαβής ἐστι.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hē tōn mēden prosēkontōn epicheirēsis ou monon asymphoros, alla kai epiblabēs esti.
sentences.l: The story shows that the taking in hand of things that belong to one in nothing is not only unprofitable but also harmful.
sentences.n: The noun ἐπιχείρησις answers the monkey's own ἐπεχείρουν, so the moral is spoken in his words. τῶν μηδὲν προσηκόντων is the same standing phrase as at fable 303.
